transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-04
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Aaron (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Liam (Orion CTO), Sara (Head of ML), Ravi (Eng Mgr), Emily (Security)

Summary: initial model-selection discovery. Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for a multi-lingual, tool-calling chat assistant with 100k+ context needs for long medical records. Discussed open-model tradeoffs, quantization, latency/cost, security (KMS, SOC2), and next steps for a benchmark.

00:00 Aaron (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro - I'm Aaron, AE on the Redwood account, priya's our SE, marcus will be on call for deep infra stuff.
00:13 Liam (CTO): Hey thanks, Liam here. we'll keep it tight. we want to understand model selection options, context length tradeoffs, and whether we should go hosted or Dedicated/Private.
00:28 Sara (Head of ML): yeah i put together our rough requirements - multi-lingual (EN, ES, PT), need for tool calling (search/EMR lookups), and in many flows we need context windows up to 80-120k tokens for long patient notes. latency SLOs are kinda strict for interactive use, so under 600ms token generation ideally but we can go a bit higher for long docs.
00:49 Priya (SE): cool. just to confirm, are those end-to-end response latencies or per-token? and what's expected concurrency?
00:56 Sara: response latencies end-to-end. concurrency normally small for deep record reads, maybe 5-10 concurrent, but peaks could be 40 during batch ingestion.
01:08 Marcus (Redwood): got it. on the model side, are you leaning open models only? any licensing constraints?
01:14 Ravi (Eng Mgr): open models preferred. we want to avoid restrictive terms. budget is important; we want to compare cost of hosted LLMs vs running on dedicated pools or private.
01:25 Aaron: perfect. so typical tradeoffs we see: hosted is fastest time to value; dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation; private (VPC / on-prem) gives data residency and full control and KMS/HSM integrations. for models, you can pick curated open models in our catalog — we support Llama-2/3 variants, Mistral, Falcon, MosaicML, etc.
01:46 Emily (Security): from a security angle we'll need SOC2 docs, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and KMS integration for key management. do you have on-prem options for audits?
01:58 Aaron: yes — Redwood Private includes customer-managed control plane and KMS integrations; we'll share SOC2 and compliance pack after.
02:07 Liam: great. back to model selection — we care about multilingual quality and tool-calling latency. Priya, can you run through model capabilities and context-length support?
02:16 Priya: sure. quick high level: open Llama-3 style models now have strong instruction following; Mistral and Falcon have good base throughput. In practice, for 100k+ contexts you need model variants and runtime optimizations: 1) models with native long-context training or position-embedding hacks (e.g., extended Llama variants), 2) 8-bit/4-bit quantized weights to make memory practical, and 3) runtime KV cache and chunked attention. Redwood runtime supports continuous KV caching and multiple kernel paths for execution.
02:44 Sara: is there a concrete recommendation? we were experimenting with Llama-3-70B and it blew memory for 64k context unless quantized and sharded.
02:53 Priya: yep. for 64k-128k we typically recommend either sharded Dedicated pools with 80-100GB GPU memory equivalents (A[100] or H100 style), or using model variants that support chunked attention like LongFormer-ish modifications. Some customers prefer to split logic: use a retrieval+rerank + short-context model for most interactions and fall back to a long-context specialized path for full document summarization.
03:20 Marcus: technically, running an off-the-shelf 70B for 128k without specialized kernels gets expensive. Redwood can route requests so that sensitive/patient-data routes go to Private dedicated instances with KMS, while low-risk calls use hosted cheaper models.
03:39 Ravi: tool-calling — we need function-like calls to do EMR lookups and live query to our search index. which models support structured tool calling?
03:47 Priya: we support function/tool-calling at the API layer; for structured outputs, some models are better at deterministic JSON generation. We often recommend instruction-tuned variants (e.g., Llama-3-instruct style or Mistral-instruct) for tool-calling reliability. Redwood also provides schema-enforced post-processing and output validators so if model drifts we can catch malformed payloads.
04:12 Sara: and multilingual — we've got Spanish + Portuguese and some medical jargon. do we need region-specific models?
04:20 Aaron: many open models have decent multilingual coverage but few excel in domain-specific medical language. you'll likely need fine-tuning or RAG with domain-specific embeddings. Redwood supports embedding store integrations; we can run evaluations across a couple models with your data.
04:34 Liam: what's the difference in latency between hosted vs dedicated for the same model?
04:40 Marcus: hosted is multi-tenant and optimized but we cannot guarantee instance-level isolation; latency SLOs are lower for Dedicated (SLA-backed). In practice, dedicated endpoints with reserved GPU capacity will reduce p99 latency significantly under load. For single request latency, hosted may be similar, but under concurrency dedicated wins.
05:00 Ravi: cost wise — any ballpark on token costs for 70B quantized vs lighter models?
05:06 Aaron: we can share a pricing grid. rough rule: larger models and larger context windows drive cost superlinearly — memory, IO, and KV cache matter. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization and batching configs to lower unit cost. we'll send examples based on your logs.
05:25 Emily: about compliance, do you persist logs or transcripts? we need audit logging but certain PHI cannot leave our VPC.
05:33 Priya: you can configure data retention at route level. Private deployment options allow customer-managed storage; Dedicated gives stronger isolation and can be configured for shorter retention. we also integrate customer KMS keys so model payloads can be encrypted at rest.
05:49 Sara: are there known model differences for tool calling accuracy? like Mistral vs Llama-3?
05:55 Priya: Mistral-instruct variants are strong on step-by-step and code-like outputs, which helps deterministic tool-calling. Llama-3-instruct is good at instruction-following and has a broader community toolchain. we usually run side-by-side evals on your prompts; sometimes a smaller fine-tuned model with prompt engineering beats a bigger general model for tool-calling reliability.
06:18 Liam: ok, can you outline a proposed pilot? we want to evaluate cost, latency, multilingual Q/A, and function-calling reliability.
06:26 Aaron: proposed pilot: 1) Redwood provisions a Dedicated pool for 2 weeks with a chosen open model (we'll propose 2 candidates), 2) run benchmarks using your de-identified logs for latency/p99/cost across 32k and 128k contexts, 3) evaluate tool-calling reliability on 50 representative flows and measure schema pass rate, 4) review security integration (KMS, SSO) — all shared in a results deck.
06:48 Sara: timeline wise we need results before end of month. is that feasible?
06:52 Priya: with logs and test prompts by 3/5 we can run a short bench and deliver initial results in a week.
07:00 Aaron: sounds good. one note: for 128k contexts some customers do a hybrid approach (RAG + long-context specialized model) to reduce cost. we'll show that in the pilot too.
07:14 Ravi: about on-prem — if we go Private, what's the support model and time to deploy?
07:20 Marcus: Private typically takes longer (2-8 weeks depending on infra), and we do a joint deployment with your infra team. Dedicated is quicker (days/weeks) and can be reserved on cloud GPUs. Private gives you full control for audits.
07:33 Emily: SSO and RBAC — can we provision role-based controls per environment and do you support SCIM user sync?
07:40 Aaron: yes, SSO/SAML + SCIM and fine-grained RBAC are available for enterprise plans. we'll share the admin docs.
07:48 Liam: any gotchas about quantization/accuracy tradeoffs?
07:52 Priya: lower-bit quantization (4-bit) can slightly reduce generation quality on certain fine-grained medical terminology; that is why we run evals on your prompts. sometimes per-layer mixed precision and calibration helps. Redwood Optimize suggests model + quant profile combos for your workload.
08:10 Sara: okay that's helpful. can we also measure multilingual hallucination rates?
08:14 Priya: yes — we'll include multilingual prompt sets and hallucination/accuracy metrics in the eval.
08:20 Aaron: quick clarification on billing model for the pilot — we can do a time-boxed Dedicated trial with usage caps or run hosted evaluation credits if you want faster setup.
08:30 Liam: we'll prefer Dedicated trial to get realistic latency numbers.
08:34 Aaron: noted. we'll propose cost for a 2-week Dedicated trial and include estimated cost for 32k vs 128k traces.
08:42 Ravi: one more question on model upgrades — can we pin model versions and roll back?
08:46 Marcus: yes, the platform supports pinning versions, canary rollouts, and automatic fallback to a compatible variant.
08:52 Sara: great. any sample artifacts you'll share?
08:55 Aaron: we'll send: pricing grid, SOC2/compliance pack, benchmark plan, and a short how-to for sending de-identified logs.
09:03 Liam: what's the best way to share logs securely? S3 with pre-signed links or via VPC peering?
09:09 Priya: either works. for Private we can do direct VPC peering or a secure connector; for initial bench, pre-signed S3 links are simplest.
09:16 Emily: make sure retention and AES-KMS encryption are called out.
09:19 Aaron: will do.
09:22 --rapid recap--
09:23 Aaron: next steps recap: Redwood to share Dedicated pricing and benchmark plan; Priya to draft the bench for 32k/128k + tool-calling tests; customer to provide de-id logs and concurrency expectations.
09:36 Liam: good. thanks everyone.
09:38 Aaron: thanks -- we'll follow up with calendar invite for the technical deep dive.
09:44 End of call.
